body.en: While single integrals accumulate quantities along one-dimensional intervals, multiple integrals accumulate continuous functions over multidimensional spatial domains. A double integral measures the net volume trapped beneath a bivariate surface \(z = f(x, y)\), total mass across variable surface density, or planar probability distributions. Through Fubini's Theorem and the Jacobian determinant, multivariable integration transforms complex domains into computable iterated operations.
body.ar: While single التكاملات accumulate quantities along one-dimensional intervals, multiple integrals accumulate continuous الدوال over multidimensional spatial domains. A double التكامل measures the net الحجم trapped beneath a bivariate surface \(z = f(x, y)\), total mass across المتغير surface density, or planar الاحتمال distributions. Through Fubini's مبرهنة and the Jacobian المحدد, multivariable integration transforms complex domains into computable iterated operations.

body.en:
Let \(f: R \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}\) be bounded on a closed, bounded region \(R\). Partition \(R\) into \(m \times n\) sub-rectangles \(R_{ij}\) of area \(\Delta A_{ij} = \Delta x_i \Delta y_j\). Choose a sample point \((x_{ij}^*, y_{ij}^*) \in R_{ij}\).

The double Riemann integral of \(f\) over \(R\) is the limit of the double Riemann sums as the partition norm \(\|P\| = \max(\Delta x_i, \Delta y_j) \to 0\):

\[ \iint_R f(x, y)\,dA = \lim_{\|P\| \to 0} \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n f(x_{ij}^*, y_{ij}^*)\,\Delta A_{ij} \]

If \(f(x, y) \ge 0\), the double integral represents the exact three-dimensional volume of the solid cylinder beneath the surface \(z = f(x, y)\) and above \(R\).
body.ar:
Let \(f: R \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}\) be bounded on a closed, bounded region \(R\). Partition \(R\) into \(m \times n\) sub-rectangles \(R_{ij}\) of المساحة \(\Delta A_{ij} = \Delta x_i \Delta y_j\). Choose a sample point \((x_{ij}^*, y_{ij}^*) \in R_{ij}\).

The double Riemann integral of \(f\) over \(R\) is the النهاية of the double Riemann sums as the partition norm \(\|P\| = \max(\Delta x_i, \Delta y_j) \to 0\):

\[ \iint_R f(x, y)\,dA = \lim_{\|P\| \to 0} \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j=1}^n f(x_{ij}^*, y_{ij}^*)\,\Delta A_{ij} \]

If \(f(x, y) \ge 0\), the double التكامل represents the exact three-dimensional الحجم of the solid cylinder beneath the surface \(z = f(x, y)\) and above \(R\).

label.en: ▲ Theorem 14.1 — Fubini's Theorem on Rectangular Domains
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 14.1 — Fubini's مبرهنة on Rectangular Domains

body.en:
Let \(f(x, y)\) be continuous on the closed rectangle \(R = [a, b] \times [c, d]\). Then the double integral equals the iterated single-variable integrals in either order:

\[ \iint_R f(x, y)\,dA = \int_a^b \left( \int_c^d f(x, y)\,dy \right) dx = \int_c^d \left( \int_a^b f(x, y)\,dx \right) dy \]

Furthermore, if the integrand factors into single-variable components \(f(x, y) = g(x)\,h(y)\), the double integral factors into the product of two independent single integrals:

\[ \iint_R g(x)h(y)\,dA = \left( \int_a^b g(x)\,dx \right) \left( \int_c^d h(y)\,dy \right) \]

Analytical Proof via Cavalieri's Principle & Slicing

Let \(V\) be the volume beneath \(z = f(x, y) \ge 0\) over \(R = [a, b] \times [c, d]\). Slicing the solid by a vertical plane perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis at a fixed position \(x\) produces a planar cross-section running from \(y = c\) to \(y = d\).

By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for single-variable functions, the cross-sectional area is:

\[ A(x) = \int_c^d f(x, y)\,dy \]

By Cavalieri's Principle and single-variable volume accumulation, the total volume is the integral of cross-sectional area across \([a, b]\):

\[ V = \int_a^b A(x)\,dx = \int_a^b \left( \int_c^d f(x, y)\,dy \right) dx \]

Similarly, slicing by planes perpendicular to the \(y\)-axis at a fixed \(y\) yields cross-sectional area \(B(y) = \int_a^b f(x, y)\,dx\), and integrating over \([c, d]\) gives:

\[ V = \int_c^d B(y)\,dy = \int_c^d \left( \int_a^b f(x, y)\,dx \right) dy \]

Because \(f\) is continuous on a compact set, it is uniformly continuous, ensuring both iterated integrals converge to the exact same double Riemann integral \(\iint_R f\,dA\) \quad \blacksquare \]
body.ar:
Let \(f(x, y)\) be continuous on the closed rectangle \(R = [a, b] \times [c, d]\). Then the double التكامل equals the iterated single-المتغير التكاملات in either order:

\[ \iint_R f(x, y)\,dA = \int_a^b \left( \int_c^d f(x, y)\,dy \right) dx = \int_c^d \left( \int_a^b f(x, y)\,dx \right) dy \]

Furthermore, if the integrand factors into single-المتغير components \(f(x, y) = g(x)\,h(y)\), the double التكامل factors into the product of two independent single التكاملات:

\[ \iint_R g(x)h(y)\,dA = \left( \int_a^b g(x)\,dx \right) \left( \int_c^d h(y)\,dy \right) \]

Analytical برهان via Cavalieri's Principle & Slicing

Let \(V\) be the الحجم beneath \(z = f(x, y) \ge 0\) over \(R = [a, b] \times [c, d]\). Slicing the solid by a vertical plane perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis at a fixed position \(x\) produces a planar cross-section running from \(y = c\) to \(y = d\).

By the Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل for single-المتغير الدوال, the cross-sectional المساحة is:

\[ A(x) = \int_c^d f(x, y)\,dy \]

By Cavalieri's Principle and single-المتغير الحجم accumulation, the total الحجم is the التكامل of cross-sectional المساحة across \([a, b]\):

\[ V = \int_a^b A(x)\,dx = \int_a^b \left( \int_c^d f(x, y)\,dy \right) dx \]

Similarly, slicing by planes perpendicular to the \(y\)-axis at a fixed \(y\) yields cross-sectional المساحة \(B(y) = \int_a^b f(x, y)\,dx\), and integrating over \([c, d]\) gives:

\[ V = \int_c^d B(y)\,dy = \int_c^d \left( \int_a^b f(x, y)\,dx \right) dy \]

Because \(f\) is continuous on a compact set, it is uniformly continuous, ensuring both iterated التكاملات converge to the exact same double Riemann التكامل \(\iint_R f\,dA\) \quad \blacksquare \]

label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Multiple التكاملات)

body.en:
Why Orthogonal Projection & Eigenvalue Characteristic Equations Work: Decompose \(\mathbf{u} = c\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w}\) where \(\mathbf{w} \perp \mathbf{v}\). Taking the dot product with \(\mathbf{v}\) uses \(\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) to isolate \(c\):

\[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = c(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{v}) + 0 \implies c = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{\|\mathbf{v}\|^2} \]

For eigenvalues, \(A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}\) with \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) is equivalent to \((A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}\). A homogeneous linear system has a non-trivial nullspace vector \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) if and only if the matrix \(A - \lambda I\) is singular, yielding the characteristic polynomial \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).
body.ar:
Why Orthogonal Projection & Eigenvalue Characteristic المعادلات Work: Decompose \(\mathbf{u} = c\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w}\) حيث \(\mathbf{w} \perp \mathbf{v}\). Taking the dot product with \(\mathbf{v}\) uses \(\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) to isolate \(c\):

\[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = c(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{v}) + 0 \implies c = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{\|\mathbf{v}\|^2} \]

For القيم الذاتية, \(A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}\) with \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) is equivalent to \((A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}\). A homogeneous linear system has a non-trivial nullspace المتجه \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) if and only if the المصفوفة \(A - \lambda I\) is singular, yielding the characteristic كثيرة الحدود \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).

body.en:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \iint_R (2x + 6x^2 y)\,dA\) over the rectangle \(R = [0, 2] \times [1, 3]\).

Step 1: Set up iterated integral.

\[ I = \int_0^2 \int_1^3 (2x + 6x^2 y)\,dy\,dx \]

Step 2: Evaluate inner integral with respect to \(y\) (holding \(x\) constant).

\[ \int_1^3 (2x + 6x^2 y)\,dy = \left[ 2xy + 3x^2 y^2 \right]_{y=1}^{y=3} = \big(6x + 3x^2(9)\big) - \big(2x + 3x^2(1)\big) = (6x + 27x^2) - (2x + 3x^2) = 4x + 24x^2 \]

Step 3: Evaluate outer integral with respect to \(x\).

\[ I = \int_0^2 (4x + 24x^2)\,dx = \left[ 2x^2 + 8x^3 \right]_0^2 = 2(2^2) + 8(2^3) = 2(4) + 8(8) = 8 + 64 = 72 \]
body.ar:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \iint_R (2x + 6x^2 y)\,dA\) over the rectangle \(R = [0, 2] \times [1, 3]\).

Step 1: Set up iterated التكامل.

\[ I = \int_0^2 \int_1^3 (2x + 6x^2 y)\,dy\,dx \]

Step 2: احسب قيمة inner التكامل بالنسبة إلى \(y\) (holding \(x\) الثابت).

\[ \int_1^3 (2x + 6x^2 y)\,dy = \left[ 2xy + 3x^2 y^2 \right]_{y=1}^{y=3} = \big(6x + 3x^2(9)\big) - \big(2x + 3x^2(1)\big) = (6x + 27x^2) - (2x + 3x^2) = 4x + 24x^2 \]

Step 3: احسب قيمة outer التكامل بالنسبة إلى \(x\).

\[ I = \int_0^2 (4x + 24x^2)\,dx = \left[ 2x^2 + 8x^3 \right]_0^2 = 2(2^2) + 8(2^3) = 2(4) + 8(8) = 8 + 64 = 72 \]

body.en:
Problem (Hard): Consider the region \(R\) in the \(xy\)-plane bounded by the curves \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 4\). What is the area of this region?

Step-by-Step Solution: The area of the region bounded by two curves \(y = f(x)\) and \(y = g(x)\) from \(x=a\) to \(x=b\), where \(f(x) \ge g(x)\) on \([a, b]\), is given by the integral \(\int_a^b (f(x) - g(x)) dx\). First, we find the intersection points of \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 4\) by setting them equal: \(x^2 = 4\), which gives \(x = -2\) and \(x = 2\). So, our limits of integration are \(a=-2\) and \(b=2\). On the interval \([-2, 2]\), the line \(y=4\) is above the parabola \(y=x^2\). Therefore, the area \(A\) is given by: \(A = \int_{-2}^{2} (4 - x^2) dx\) Now, we evaluate the integral: \(A = \left[ 4x - \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{-2}^{2}\) \(A = \left( 4(2) - \frac{(2)^3}{3} \right) - \left( 4(-2) - \frac{(-2)^3}{3} \right)\) \(A = \left( 8 - \frac{8}{3} \right) - \left( -8 - \frac{-8}{3} \right)\) \(A = \left( 8 - \frac{8}{3} \right) - \left( -8 + \frac{8}{3} \right)\) \(A = 8 - \frac{8}{3} + 8 - \frac{8}{3}\) \(A = 16 - \frac{16}{3}\) \(A = \frac{48}{3} - \frac{16}{3}\) \(A = \frac{32}{3}\) Therefore, the area of the region is \(\frac{32}{3}\).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): Consider the region \(R\) in the \(xy\)-plane bounded by the curves \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 4\). What is the المساحة of this region?

Step-by-Step الحل: The المساحة of the region bounded by two curves \(y = f(x)\) and \(y = g(x)\) from \(x=a\) to \(x=b\), حيث \(f(x) \ge g(x)\) on \([a, b]\), is المعطيات by the التكامل \(\int_a^b (f(x) - g(x)) dx\). First, we أوجد التقاطع points of \(y = x^2\) and \(y = 4\) by setting them equal: \(x^2 = 4\), which gives \(x = -2\) and \(x = 2\). So, our النهايات of integration are \(a=-2\) and \(b=2\). On the interval \([-2, 2]\), the line \(y=4\) is above the القطع المكافئ \(y=x^2\). وبالتالي, the المساحة \(A\) is المعطيات by: \(A = \int_{-2}^{2} (4 - x^2) dx\) Now, we احسب قيمة التكامل: \(A = \left[ 4x - \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{-2}^{2}\) \(A = \left( 4(2) - \frac{(2)^3}{3} \right) - \left( 4(-2) - \frac{(-2)^3}{3} \right)\) \(A = \left( 8 - \frac{8}{3} \right) - \left( -8 - \frac{-8}{3} \right)\) \(A = \left( 8 - \frac{8}{3} \right) - \left( -8 + \frac{8}{3} \right)\) \(A = 8 - \frac{8}{3} + 8 - \frac{8}{3}\) \(A = 16 - \frac{16}{3}\) \(A = \frac{48}{3} - \frac{16}{3}\) \(A = \frac{32}{3}\) وبالتالي, the المساحة of the region is \(\frac{32}{3}\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \iint_R (2x + y)\,dA\) where \(R\) is the rectangular region \([0, 3] \times [1, 2]\).
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations
احسب قيمة \(\displaystyle \iint_R (2x + y)\,dA\) حيث \(R\) is the rectangular region \([0, 3] \times [1, 2]\).

solution.en:
Set up iterated integral:
\[ \int_1^2 \int_0^3 (2x + y)\,dx\,dy = \int_1^2 \left[ x^2 + xy \right]_0^3 dy = \int_1^2 (9 + 3y)\,dy \]
Integrate with respect to \(y\):
\[ \left[ 9y + \frac{3y^2}{2} \right]_1^2 = \left(18 + \frac{12}{2}\right) - \left(9 + \frac{3}{2}\right) = 24 - 10.5 = 13.5 = \frac{27}{2} \]

label.en: ▲ Theorem 14.2 — General Bounded Regions (Type I / Type II) & Order Reversal
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 14.2 — General Bounded Regions (Type I / Type II) & Order Reversal

body.en:
When integrating over non-rectangular planar domains \(D\):

  • Type I (Vertically Simple): \(D = \{ (x, y) : a \le x \le b,\; g_1(x) \le y \le g_2(x) \}\):
    \[ \iint_D f(x, y)\,dA = \int_a^b \left( \int_{g_1(x)}^{g_2(x)} f(x, y)\,dy \right) dx \]
  • Type II (Horizontally Simple): \(D = \{ (x, y) : c \le y \le d,\; h_1(y) \le x \le h_2(y) \}\):
    \[ \iint_D f(x, y)\,dA = \int_c^d \left( \int_{h_1(y)}^{h_2(y)} f(x, y)\,dx \right) dy \]

Reversing the Order of Integration: Integrands whose single-variable antiderivatives are non-elementary (such as \(e^{x^2}\), \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\), or \(\cos(y^2)\)) can often be evaluated by sketching the region \(D\) and switching the slicing orientation from vertical to horizontal (or vice versa).

label.ar: مثال محلول 14.2 — Medium: Reversing Order of Integration for Non-Elementary Antiderivatives

body.en:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^1 \int_y^1 e^{x^2}\,dx\,dy\).

Step 1: Sketch and analyze the integration domain.
The current bounds are: inner \(y \le x \le 1\), outer \(0 \le y \le 1\).
This is a triangle bounded by the lines \(x = y\), \(x = 1\), and the \(x\)-axis \(y = 0\).

Step 2: Re-express the domain as a Type I region.
For each vertical slice from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 1\), \(y\) runs from \(y = 0\) (bottom) to \(y = x\) (top):

\[ D = \{ (x, y) : 0 \le x \le 1,\; 0 \le y \le x \} \]

Step 3: Setup and evaluate the reversed iterated integral.

\[ \int_0^1 \int_0^x e^{x^2}\,dy\,dx = \int_0^1 \left[ y e^{x^2} \right]_{y=0}^{y=x} dx = \int_0^1 x e^{x^2}\,dx \]

Now substitute \(u = x^2\), \(du = 2x\,dx\):

\[ \int_0^1 x e^{x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2} \left[ e^{x^2} \right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{2}(e^1 - e^0) = \frac{e - 1}{2} \]
body.ar:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \int_0^1 \int_y^1 e^{x^2}\,dx\,dy\).

Step 1: Sketch and analyze the integration المجال.
The current bounds are: inner \(y \le x \le 1\), outer \(0 \le y \le 1\).
This is a المثلث bounded by the lines \(x = y\), \(x = 1\), and the \(x\)-axis \(y = 0\).

Step 2: Re-express the المجال as a Type I region.
For each vertical slice from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 1\), \(y\) runs from \(y = 0\) (bottom) to \(y = x\) (top):

\[ D = \{ (x, y) : 0 \le x \le 1,\; 0 \le y \le x \} \]

Step 3: Setup and احسب قيمة reversed iterated التكامل.

\[ \int_0^1 \int_0^x e^{x^2}\,dy\,dx = \int_0^1 \left[ y e^{x^2} \right]_{y=0}^{y=x} dx = \int_0^1 x e^{x^2}\,dx \]

Now عوّض \(u = x^2\), \(du = 2x\,dx\):

\[ \int_0^1 x e^{x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2} \left[ e^{x^2} \right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{2}(e^1 - e^0) = \frac{e - 1}{2} \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium
Evaluate the iterated integral by reversing the order of integration:
\[ \int_0^{\pi} \int_y^{\pi} \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx\,dy \]
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium
احسب قيمة the iterated integral by reversing the order of integration:
\[ \int_0^{\pi} \int_y^{\pi} \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx\,dy \]

solution.en:
The domain is \(0 \le y \le \pi\) and \(y \le x \le \pi\).
This is the triangular region bounded by \(y = 0\), \(x = \pi\), and \(y = x\).
Reversing order to Type I: \(x\) ranges from \(0\) to \(\pi\), while \(y\) ranges from \(0\) to \(x\):
\[ \int_0^{\pi} \int_0^x \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dy\,dx = \int_0^{\pi} \left[ y \frac{\sin x}{x} \right]_{y=0}^{y=x} dx = \int_0^{\pi} x \frac{\sin x}{x}\,dx = \int_0^{\pi} \sin x\,dx \]
\[ = \big[ -\cos x \big]_0^{\pi} = -\cos(\pi) - (-\cos 0) = -(-1) - (-1) = 1 + 1 = 2 \]

label.en: ▲ Theorem 14.3 — Polar Coordinates Transformation & The Jacobian Determinant
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 14.3 — Polar الإحداثيات Transformation & The Jacobian المحدد

body.en:
When a double integral exhibits circular symmetry (such as disks, sectors, or integrands containing \(x^2 + y^2\)), transform using polar coordinates \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\).

The differential area element is scaled by the Jacobian determinant:

\[ J(r, \theta) = \frac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(r, \theta)} = \begin{vmatrix} \frac{\partial x}{\partial r} & \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta} \\ \frac{\partial y}{\partial r} & \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta} \end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} \cos\theta & -r\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & r\cos\theta \end{vmatrix} = r\cos^2\theta + r\sin^2\theta = r \]

Thus the polar area element is:

\[ dA = r\,dr\,d\theta \]

and the transformation formula is:

\[ \iint_R f(x, y)\,dA = \iint_S f(r\cos\theta, r\sin\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta \]

Analytical Application — The Gaussian Integral Evaluation

Let \(I = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx\). Squaring the integral and writing as a double integral over \(\mathbb{R}^2\):

\[ I^2 = \left( \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx \right) \left( \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-y^2}\,dy \right) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-(x^2 + y^2)}\,dx\,dy \]

Transforming into polar coordinates over the entire plane \(0 \le \theta \le 2\pi\), \(0 \le r < \infty\):

\[ I^2 = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^\infty e^{-r^2}\,r\,dr\,d\theta = \left( \int_0^{2\pi} d\theta \right) \left( \int_0^\infty r e^{-r^2}\,dr \right) \]\[ = 2\pi \left[ -\frac{1}{2}e^{-r^2} \right]_0^\infty = 2\pi \left( 0 - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \right) = 2\pi \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \pi \]

Taking the square root establishes the famous exact Gaussian value: \(I = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx = \sqrt{\pi}\) \quad \blacksquare \]
body.ar:
When a double التكامل exhibits circular symmetry (such as disks, sectors, or integrands containing \(x^2 + y^2\)), transform using polar الإحداثيات \(x = r\cos\theta\), \(y = r\sin\theta\).

The differential المساحة element is scaled by the Jacobian determinant:

\[ J(r, \theta) = \frac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(r, \theta)} = \begin{vmatrix} \frac{\partial x}{\partial r} & \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta} \\ \frac{\partial y}{\partial r} & \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta} \end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} \cos\theta & -r\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & r\cos\theta \end{vmatrix} = r\cos^2\theta + r\sin^2\theta = r \]

Thus the polar المساحة element is:

\[ dA = r\,dr\,d\theta \]

and the transformation الصيغة is:

\[ \iint_R f(x, y)\,dA = \iint_S f(r\cos\theta, r\sin\theta)\,r\,dr\,d\theta \]

Analytical Application — The Gaussian التكامل Evaluation

Let \(I = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx\). Squaring the التكامل and writing as a double التكامل over \(\mathbb{R}^2\):

\[ I^2 = \left( \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx \right) \left( \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-y^2}\,dy \right) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-(x^2 + y^2)}\,dx\,dy \]

Transforming into polar الإحداثيات over the entire plane \(0 \le \theta \le 2\pi\), \(0 \le r < \infty\):

\[ I^2 = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^\infty e^{-r^2}\,r\,dr\,d\theta = \left( \int_0^{2\pi} d\theta \right) \left( \int_0^\infty r e^{-r^2}\,dr \right) \]\[ = 2\pi \left[ -\frac{1}{2}e^{-r^2} \right]_0^\infty = 2\pi \left( 0 - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \right) = 2\pi \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \pi \]

Taking the square root establishes the famous exact Gaussian value: \(I = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}\,dx = \sqrt{\pi}\) \quad \blacksquare \]

label.en: Worked Example 14.3 — Advanced: Volume Under Paraboloid via Polar Double Integral
label.ar: مثال محلول 14.3 — Advanced: الحجم Under Paraboloid via Polar Double التكامل

body.en:
Find the volume of the solid bounded above by the paraboloid \(z = 9 - x^2 - y^2\) and below by the \(xy\)-plane.

Step 1: Determine the planar boundary in the \(xy\)-plane.
Set \(z = 0\): \(9 - x^2 - y^2 = 0 \implies x^2 + y^2 = 9\).
The base is the disk \(D\) of radius \(R = 3\) centered at the origin.

Step 2: Convert to polar coordinates.
In polar coordinates: \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\), so \(z = 9 - r^2\).
Limits: \(0 \le r \le 3\), \(0 \le \theta \le 2\pi\).
Area element: \(dA = r\,dr\,d\theta\).

Step 3: Setup and evaluate the integral.

\[ V = \iint_D (9 - x^2 - y^2)\,dA = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^3 (9 - r^2)r\,dr\,d\theta = \left( \int_0^{2\pi} d\theta \right) \left( \int_0^3 (9r - r^3)\,dr \right) \]\[ = 2\pi \left[ \frac{9r^2}{2} - \frac{r^4}{4} \right]_0^3 = 2\pi \left( \frac{9(9)}{2} - \frac{81}{4} \right) = 2\pi \left( \frac{162 - 81}{4} \right) = 2\pi \left( \frac{81}{4} \right) = \frac{81\pi}{2} \]
body.ar:
Find the الحجم of the solid bounded above by the paraboloid \(z = 9 - x^2 - y^2\) and below by the \(xy\)-plane.

Step 1: حدّد planar boundary in the \(xy\)-plane.
Set \(z = 0\): \(9 - x^2 - y^2 = 0 \implies x^2 + y^2 = 9\).
The base is the disk \(D\) of نصف القطر \(R = 3\) centered at the origin.

Step 2: Convert to polar الإحداثيات.
In polar الإحداثيات: \(x^2 + y^2 = r^2\), so \(z = 9 - r^2\).
Limits: \(0 \le r \le 3\), \(0 \le \theta \le 2\pi\).
Area element: \(dA = r\,dr\,d\theta\).

Step 3: Setup and احسب قيمة التكامل.

\[ V = \iint_D (9 - x^2 - y^2)\,dA = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^3 (9 - r^2)r\,dr\,d\theta = \left( \int_0^{2\pi} d\theta \right) \left( \int_0^3 (9r - r^3)\,dr \right) \]\[ = 2\pi \left[ \frac{9r^2}{2} - \frac{r^4}{4} \right]_0^3 = 2\pi \left( \frac{9(9)}{2} - \frac{81}{4} \right) = 2\pi \left( \frac{162 - 81}{4} \right) = 2\pi \left( \frac{81}{4} \right) = \frac{81\pi}{2} \]

body.en:
Polar Area Element (Jacobian r): In polar coordinates, \(dA = r\,dr\,d\theta\). Omitting the extra factor of \(r\) is the single most common error in multivariable calculus!

Reversing Order of Integration: You CANNOT merely swap the integral signs and limits when the region is non-rectangular: \(\int_0^1 \int_x^1 f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \ne \int_x^1 \int_0^1 f(x,y)\,dx\,dy\). You MUST sketch the 2D domain and reconstruct the bounding functions from horizontal vs vertical slices.

Coordinate Transformations Jacobian: When substituting \(x = g(u, v)\), \(y = h(u, v)\), always multiply the integrand by the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant \(|J(u, v)| = |x_u y_v - x_v y_u|\).

Polar Radius Limits: The radial coordinate \(r\) measures distance from the origin and is always non-negative: \(r \ge 0\). Setting negative lower limits on \(r\) invalidates the transformation.
body.ar:
Polar المساحة Element (Jacobian r): In polar الإحداثيات, \(dA = r\,dr\,d\theta\). Omitting the extra factor of \(r\) is the single most common error in multivariable التفاضل والتكامل!

Reversing Order of Integration: You CANNOT merely swap the التكامل signs and النهايات عندما the region is non-rectangular: \(\int_0^1 \int_x^1 f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \ne \int_x^1 \int_0^1 f(x,y)\,dx\,dy\). You MUST sketch the 2D المجال and reconstruct the bounding الدوال from horizontal vs vertical slices.

Coordinate Transformations Jacobian: عندما substituting \(x = g(u, v)\), \(y = h(u, v)\), always multiply the integrand by the absolute value of the Jacobian المحدد \(|J(u, v)| = |x_u y_v - x_v y_u|\).

Polar نصف القطر النهايات: The radial الإحداثي \(r\) measures distance from the origin and is always non-negative: \(r \ge 0\). Setting negative lower النهايات on \(r\) invalidates the transformation.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced
Evaluate the double integral \(\displaystyle \iint_D e^{x^2 + y^2}\,dA\) where \(D\) is the semi-annular region \(\{ (x, y) : 1 \le x^2 + y^2 \le 4, y \ge 0 \}\).
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced
احسب قيمة the double integral \(\displaystyle \iint_D e^{x^2 + y^2}\,dA\) حيث \(D\) is the semi-annular region \(\{ (x, y) : 1 \le x^2 + y^2 \le 4, y \ge 0 \}\).

solution.en:
Convert the semi-annulus to polar coordinates:
Radius bounds: \(1 \le r^2 \le 4 \implies 1 \le r \le 2\).
Angle bounds (since \(y \ge 0\), upper half-plane): \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\).
Area element: \(dA = r\,dr\,d\theta\).
Set up the integral:
\[ \iint_D e^{x^2 + y^2}\,dA = \int_0^{\pi} \int_1^2 e^{r^2}\,r\,dr\,d\theta = \left( \int_0^\pi d\theta \right) \left( \int_1^2 r e^{r^2}\,dr \right) \]
Substitute \(u = r^2 \implies du = 2r\,dr\):
\[ = \pi \left[ \frac{1}{2}e^{r^2} \right]_1^2 = \frac{\pi}{2}(e^4 - e^1) = \frac{\pi e(e^3 - 1)}{2} \]

question.en: Consider the solid \(E\) bounded by the surfaces \(z = x^2 + y^2\) and \(z = 8 - x^2 - y^2\). Calculate the volume of this solid using a triple integral by first transforming to cylindrical coordinates. Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).
question.ar: Consider the solid \(E\) bounded بتطبيق surfaces \(z = x^2 + y^2\) and \(z = 8 - x^2 - y^2\). احسب volume of this solid using a triple integral by first transforming to cylindrical coordinates. Express your answer in terms of \(\pi\).

hints.en: The solid \(E\) is bounded below by the paraboloid \(z = x^2 + y^2\) and above by the paraboloid \(z = 8 - x^2 - y^2\). To find the intersection of these two surfaces, we set them equal: \(x^2 + y^2 = 8 - x^2 - y^2\), which simplifies to \(2(x^2 + y^2) = 8\), or \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\). This is a circle of radius 2 in the \(xy\)-plane.

hints.en: First, integrate with respect to \(z\): \(\int_{r^2}^{8-r^2} r \, dz = r [z]_{r^2}^{8-r^2} = r (8-r^2 - r^2) = r(8 - 2r^2) = 8r - 2r^3\).
hints.ar: First, integrate بالنسبة إلى \(z\): \(\int_{r^2}^{8-r^2} r \, dz = r [z]_{r^2}^{8-r^2} = r (8-r^2 - r^2) = r(8 - 2r^2) = 8r - 2r^3\).

hints.en: Therefore, the volume of the solid is \(16\pi\).

solution.en:
The solid \(E\) is bounded below by the paraboloid \(z = x^2 + y^2\) and above by the paraboloid \(z = 8 - x^2 - y^2\). To find the intersection of these two surfaces, we set them equal: \(x^2 + y^2 = 8 - x^2 - y^2\), which simplifies to \(2(x^2 + y^2) = 8\), or \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\). This is a circle of radius 2 in the \(xy\)-plane. 

In cylindrical coordinates, \(x = r \cos(\theta)\), \(y = r \sin(\theta)\), and \(z = z\). The equations of the surfaces become \(z = r^2\) and \(z = 8 - r^2\). The intersection occurs at \(r^2 = 8 - r^2\), so \(2r^2 = 8\), which gives \(r^2 = 4\), and thus \(r = 2\). The range for \(\theta\) is \(0 \le \theta \le 2\pi\). The range for \(z\) is \(r^2 \le z \le 8 - r^2\). The volume element in cylindrical coordinates is \(dV = r \, dz \, dr \, d\theta\). 

The volume \(V\) is given by the triple integral:
\[ V = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^2 \int_{r^2}^{8-r^2} r \, dz \, dr \, d\theta \] 
First, integrate with respect to \(z\): 
\[ \int_{r^2}^{8-r^2} r \, dz = r [z]_{r^2}^{8-r^2} = r (8-r^2 - r^2) = r(8 - 2r^2) = 8r - 2r^3 \] 
Next, integrate with respect to \(r\): 
\[ \int_0^2 (8r - 2r^3) \, dr = \left[ 4r^2 - \frac{1}{2}r^4 \right]_0^2 = (4(2^2) - \frac{1}{2}(2^4)) - (0) = (16 - \frac{1}{2}(16)) = 16 - 8 = 8 \] 
Finally, integrate with respect to \(\theta\): 
\[ V = \int_0^{2\pi} 8 \, d\theta = 8 [\theta]_0^{2\pi} = 8(2\pi - 0) = 16\pi \] 
Therefore, the volume of the solid is \(16\pi\).
solution.ar:
The solid \(E\) is bounded below بتطبيق paraboloid \(z = x^2 + y^2\) and above بتطبيق paraboloid \(z = 8 - x^2 - y^2\). To أوجد intersection of these two surfaces, we set them equal: \(x^2 + y^2 = 8 - x^2 - y^2\), which simplإذا كانies to \(2(x^2 + y^2) = 8\), or \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\). This is a circle of radius 2 in the \(xy\)-plane. 

In cylindrical coordinates, \(x = r \cos(\theta)\), \(y = r \sin(\theta)\), and \(z = z\). The equations of the surfaces become \(z = r^2\) and \(z = 8 - r^2\). The intersection occurs at \(r^2 = 8 - r^2\), so \(2r^2 = 8\), which gives \(r^2 = 4\), and thus \(r = 2\). The range for \(\theta\) is \(0 \le \theta \le 2\pi\). The range for \(z\) is \(r^2 \le z \le 8 - r^2\). The volume element in cylindrical coordinates is \(dV = r \, dz \, dr \, d\theta\). 

The volume \(V\) is given بتطبيق triple integral:
\[ V = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^2 \int_{r^2}^{8-r^2} r \, dz \, dr \, d\theta \] 
First, integrate بالنسبة إلى \(z\): 
\[ \int_{r^2}^{8-r^2} r \, dz = r [z]_{r^2}^{8-r^2} = r (8-r^2 - r^2) = r(8 - 2r^2) = 8r - 2r^3 \] 
Next, integrate بالنسبة إلى \(r\): 
\[ \int_0^2 (8r - 2r^3) \, dr = \left[ 4r^2 - \frac{1}{2}r^4 \right]_0^2 = (4(2^2) - \frac{1}{2}(2^4)) - (0) = (16 - \frac{1}{2}(16)) = 16 - 8 = 8 \] 
Finally, integrate بالنسبة إلى \(\theta\): 
\[ V = \int_0^{2\pi} 8 \, d\theta = 8 [\theta]_0^{2\pi} = 8(2\pi - 0) = 16\pi \] 
وبالتالي، the volume of the solid is \(16\pi\).
